imports: role-release-evidence.candidate.json exact wrapper/current role checks and receipt-expiry cap
rules: Checkpoint service explicitly permits the selected live controller witness principal to READ_CURRENT for RELEASE_CONSUMPTION only. Its existing appointed witness signing identity authenticates RPC; it receives no ADVANCE permission, checkpoint key, store path access or consumer key.

READ_CURRENT request body includes ConsumptionReadBinding and minimum_generation/head equal the issued release's expected decision checkpoint. The exact request is durably retained in ConsumptionPreparation before send. Fresh nonce/request ID are selected for this consume attempt, not copied from the issuer.

Service verifies current caller signature, permitted operation/use, actual per-fragment credentials/PID/start, exact binding/store/clock domain, current authority and original setup deadline. Response signs request hash and nonce, so all consumption fields are transitively bound.

Service response must be PRESENT with complete history, current head exactly equal to the expected accepted decision checkpoint, and that certificate bound to the exact method decision/exposure in the release. Any later abort, changed head, expired authority, stale nonce, missing/unavailable history or changed controller/channel rejects consumption.

Controller first validates all release/custody/completion/method/role/current-authority dependencies and retains one-use preparation. Its final external evidence acquisition is its own fresh checkpoint READ_CURRENT. It authenticates that response and original-time/current-authority checks immediately before an atomic PREPARED->CONSUMED local commit.

No other blocking verification between the completed fresh read and consumption commit except the bounded exact local commit. If more I/O is needed, do not consume on the old read. Fail closed; any explicitly authorized reread retains the same consume attempt/release/clock and creates no fresh release allowance.

After commit recheck original deadlines/authority and process/channel continuity before private exposure. If commit or post-commit checks cross a deadline or become uncertain, record SPENT_NO_EXPOSURE/UNAVAILABLE and expose no private input. Commit success is not itself private-read permission.

Lost read/commit responses do not create a new release ID/consume attempt/budget or automatically resend/distribute custody. Exact retained state may be reconciled only within original validity; no automatic restart or repeated release is authorized.

This is a fresh observation plus exact local one-use commit, not a distributed transaction freezing all future checkpoint/authority changes. Later record retention supplies audit evidence, never renewed permission. Existing per-invocation role/clock guards remain.

Issuer READ_CURRENT is separately useful for issuance but never satisfies controller consumption. The controller endpoint/client descriptor and signing material are excluded from all child pass_fds/descriptor plans; absence/forwarding bounds remain under the accepted trusted-controller claim and require runtime observation.

CONSUMED_VALID requires every response/generation/head/authority/time field non-null and causally ordered; failure/uncertainty leaves unavailable fields null without fabricated timestamps. No null can satisfy the successful exposure gate.

Setup decision/current checkpoint/appointment must be valid at consumption inside the original180-second interval. The successfully consumed release authorizes only the already fixed model/global window and ongoing guards; its later model phase does not renew setup authority or permit another consumption.

Candidate03 NR01..NR12 applies before the final controller READ_CURRENT and at the prescribed postcommit guard. Wrapper/release expiry is an admission limit capped by the original setup/dependency validity, not a replacement model deadline; no fresh observation is fabricated from the wrapper itself.
